entry.title: What Drives It All: The Compliance Data Foundation in SAP S/4HANA for Product Compliance
entry.content:
This post builds on and complements a previous article in which we introduced the three core capabilities of SAP S/4HANA for Product Compliance. If you haven't read the blog post “Product Compliance in SAP S/4HANA: How Three Integrated Capabilities Enable Safe Global Operations” yet, you can find it here: Product Compliance in SAP S/4HANA: How Three Integrated Capabilities Enable Safe Global Operations

In this post, we go one level deeper and take a closer look at what drives all three capabilities: the Compliance Data Foundation.

This foundation is your single source of truth for regulatory execution. At its core: Compliance Requirements, Purposes, and Content that work together across three key capabilities: Product Marketability & Component Compliance, Dangerous Goods Management and Compliance Document Management.

The already mentioned Compliance Requirements are the semantic anchor, and deliverable building blocks that capture the obligations from a regulation, part of a regulation, or a stakeholder requirement. Think of examples like "Labeling according to GHS," or "Dangerous Goods Classification according to ADN or IATA." 

Compliance Requirements are assigned to a product through Compliance Purposes which are self-configurable bundles that group the relevant compliance requirements based on a specific obligation a company needs to fulfill. A Compliance Purpose can be created for a country, a region, a customer group, a product type, or a business process. They are highly flexible and can be defined however your use case demands.

And here is what makes the Compliance Data Foundation so powerful:
When regulations change, the update flows through the foundation straight into execution, no manual intervention across multiple places.

The result? Consistent, audit-ready compliance logic that scales with your business and keeps pace with an ever-evolving regulatory landscape.

To learn more about the Compliance Data Foundation, take a look at the new accompanying video: In brief: SAP Product Compliance - Compliance Data Foundation

entry.title: Pain Points in Sustainable Finance
entry.content:
Over the last few years, sustainability has moved from the sidelines to the CFO agenda. 

That sounds obvious now, but regulatory pressure is increasing, investors are asking tougher questions, and companies are expected to demonstrate measurable progress rather than simply publish reports. Finance teams have become central players in this shift. 

The biggest challenge isn't proving sustainability matters. It's making it operational. 

While sustainability has become a business priority, many finance teams are running into the same challenge: It's easy to agree sustainability matters. It's much harder to embed it into the way the business actually runs. 

With that, three pain points stand out.

Pain Point #1: Sustainability Data Is Everywhere, But Rarely Connected 

Most organizations don't have a sustainability ambition problem. They have a data problem.  

Financial data lives in one system. Operational data lives in another. Sustainability data often lives somewhere else entirely. Bringing everything together for reporting, planning, and analysis can require significant manual effort. 

The result is that teams spend more time reconciling information than acting on it. 

This is where SAP's ecosystem becomes especially important. Finance, operations, supply chain, and sustainability teams can't make informed decisions when data is scattered across multiple systems. By bringing these data sources together, SAP helps organizations establish a shared foundation for sustainability and business decision-making, reducing manual reconciliation and increasing confidence in the numbers being used. 

Pain Point #2: Reporting Requirements Keep Expanding 

A few years ago, many sustainability programs focused primarily on emissions reporting. Today, expectations are considerably higher. 

Organizations are managing evolving disclosure requirements, increased scrutiny around auditability, and rising demand for product-level carbon footprints. 

The challenge for finance teams isn't simply generating another report. Rather, it is creating a reporting process that is repeatable, trustworthy, and scalable as requirements continue to evolve. 

This challenge underscores the value of SAP's integrated sustainability portfolio. As regulations and disclosure requirements continue to evolve, organizations need more than another reporting tool. They need sustainability processes embedded into the systems already used to manage finance, supply chain, and operations. SAP's approach helps organizations build a reporting foundation that can scale as requirements become more complex. 

Pain Point #3: Demonstrating Business Value 

Most organizations can measure sustainability activities, while fewer can clearly connect them to business outcomes. 

Finance leaders are being asked to justify investments, prioritize initiatives, and demonstrate value. That means sustainability programs need to show how they contribute to cost reduction, operational efficiency, risk management, resilience, or growth. 

Without that connection, sustainability can feel like another reporting requirement rather than a business driver. 

That's why the conversation is increasingly shifting from: "How do we report sustainability?" to "How do we use sustainability to make better business decisions?" 

Perhaps most importantly, SAP is helping organizations bridge the gap between sustainability performance and business performance. When sustainability data is connected to financial and operational outcomes, leaders can evaluate trade-offs, prioritize investments, and measure impact with greater confidence. That's when sustainability starts to move from a cost of compliance to a driver of business value. 

What Pain Points Are You Seeing? 

As sustainability becomes more embedded in finance, new challenges continue to emerge around data, reporting, planning, and demonstrating business value. 

If you're seeing a different pain point in your organization, let me know. I'd be happy to explore it in a future post and take a closer look at how SAP solutions look to address it.

entry.title: SAP Sustainability Footprint Management: Q3-26 Updates & Highlights
entry.content:
As we move into the final stretch of 2026, I'm back with the next edition of my quarterly blog series covering the latest innovations and highlights in SAP Sustainability Footprint Management. Q3 has been a quarter of significant depth work: AI capabilities that go to the core of footprint data quality, energy management that now reaches from source composition through to disclosure-ready reporting, transport footprint calculations grounded in real-world commercial shipping routes, and usability improvements that came directly out of customer feedback. In this edition, I'm covering:

  • Improved AI-assisted Emission Factor Mapping
  • Enhanced Energy Source Management
  • Default Sea Distances for Transport Footprint Calculations
  • Customer-Driven Usability Improvements
  • Other Release Highlights
  • Upcoming Live Sessions
  • Additional Information

 

Improved AI-assisted Emission Factor Mapping

Mapping emission factors to purchased products is one of the most data-intensive steps in calculating a Scope 3.1 footprint. Organizations often manage hundreds or thousands of purchased products and product groups, each of which needs to be matched to a suitable emission factor before it can be included in footprint calculations. Doing this manually is time-consuming, and the quality of the mapping directly affects the accuracy of your results.

In Q3-26, we significantly improved how AI assists with this task in the Manage Purchased Product Footprints app. The core of the improvement is that the mapping process now uses large language models (LLMs) to enrich product classification and pre-process emission factor data packages before generating suggestions, fundamentally improving the mapping accuracy. You also get more control over the inputs: you can select which emission factor data packages to use, choose between quantity-based and spend-based footprints, and optionally provide additional context in a new Additional Information field. This is useful for enriching sparse product master data with plain-language descriptions or sourcing geography, giving the LLM more to work with. Before generating suggestions, the AI also evaluates whether it can identify your product with sufficient confidence. If the inference threshold is not met, the system sets the status to No Mappings Available rather than producing low-quality suggestions – in which case adding more detail in the Additional Information field and regenerating is the recommended path forward.

Generate Emission Factor Mappings with AI

The most visible change is in how suggestions are presented. Instead of a similarity score, each AI-generated mapping now comes with a confidence score and a natural-language reasoning. The confidence score uses a 0–10 scale (high ≥ 8, medium ≥ 6, low < 6), calculated from product name, description, commodity code, supplier location, and dataset characteristics. The reasoning explains what the AI understood about the product, why it selected a particular dataset, and where relevant why the confidence score is lower. This combination makes it much easier to judge whether a suggestion is reliable enough to release immediately or whether it needs a closer look.

AI-generated Mapping Results

To keep the review process focused, the system now shows up to three suggestions per record, down from ten previously. Each record also carries an explicit action recommendation – release, review, regenerate, or manually map – so you can triage your queue at a glance rather than reading every confidence score individually. If none of the suggestions are suitable, you can regenerate mappings without losing the existing footprint record. If you had previously generated mappings using the older AI-assisted mapping process, these are now shown with an Outdated status. You can regenerate them to take advantage of the new process, including the updated confidence scores, reasoning, and action recommendations.

For more information on AI-assisted mapping, see Using AI to Map Emission Factors to Purchased Products and Product Groups on SAP Help. To see the updated mapping process – from generating suggestions to reviewing confidence scores and releasing footprints – watch the short demo:

 

The mapping workflow in general is also now more resilient to product quantity and unit of measure conversion issues for quantity-based footprints: rather than blocking the process, the system allows you to create, import, or release a footprint and sets its status to Released with Warnings to flag any conversion gaps. Note that unresolved conversion issues will cause an error when the footprint is used in an organizational footprint inventory calculation, so it’s worth addressing them promptly. For more information, see Product Quantity Conversion Logic in Purchased Product Footprints and Warnings in Released Purchased Product Footprints on SAP Help.

Taken together, these improvements – more accurate suggestions, transparent reasoning, a streamlined review workflow, and greater resilience throughout – represent a significant step forward for anyone managing emission factor mapping at scale. But nothing validates an innovation more than hearing directly from the people whose daily work it has transformed – and the feedback coming in from customers who have already adopted the updated process, across very different industries and scales of operation, tells a consistent story of time saved, confidence gained, and pace transformed.

What customers are saying:

"Before, I was manually chasing emission factors for every single material – looking up each screw, checking the material, finding the right dataset. Now, using the emission factor mapping functionality within SAP Sustainability Footprint Management, I was able to map 1,500 materials overnight with a 100% mapping rate and 68% at high confidence."

Nadine Frank, Sustainability Controller, HARTING Technology Group

"The AI Emission Factor Mapping in SAP Sustainability Footprint Management is exceptionally well designed. The automated assignments are highly accurate, and the AI-generated rationale provides valuable transparency, making large-scale review, validation, and adjustment processes significantly more efficient."

Rosalie Schröter, Quality Specialist (IMS), Piller Blowers & Compressors GmbH

"With the latest release of SAP Sustainability Footprint Management, we saw AI emission factor mapping improve from 81% to a perfect 100% match rate – correctly mapping every record and reinforcing our confidence in AI-generated results."

Terézia Mačingová, SAP IT Business Systems Consultant, SAP SE

 

Enhanced Energy Source Management

Managing energy goes beyond tracking consumption volumes. To calculate accurate Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3.3 emissions, you need to know what your energy is made of: the renewable and fossil mix, the fuel composition, the heating value of combusted fuels, and where the energy comes from. And beyond GHG calculations, organizations need to report on their energy consumption itself: how much energy they use, broken down by source type and plant, is increasingly a core disclosure requirement under frameworks like the EU’s Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD). With a major expansion of energy source data management across multiple apps in SAP Sustainability Footprint Management, we’re enabling exactly this level of granularity end-to-end. 

The starting point is the Manage Emission Factors app, where you can now add detailed composition attributes to emission factor datasets used with energy sources. Energy Mix (Fossil, Renewable, Nuclear) and Fuel Mix (Coal, Petroleum, Natural Gas, Biomass, Biofuel, and others) are captured as percentages that must add up to 100%. You can also define Energy Content using either the Lower Heating Value (LHV) or Higher Heating Value (HHV), relevant when burning fuel to determine how much usable thermal energy is released. Both the simple and LCA import templates have been updated to support these new attributes. To make this actionable immediately, the default EPA (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency) 2024 & 2025 emission factor packages have been updated with these new characteristics where applicable. Three new packages are also now available as default content: DEFRA (UK Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs) 2025 & 2026 and EMBER 2023 & 2024 – all including Energy Mix, Energy Content, and Fuel Mix data where applicable.

In Manage Footprint Inventory Scopes, you can activate Energy Content and Energy Mix so that heating values and mix composition are included in your footprint calculations. In Manage Calculation Variants, you then define which heating value – Lower or Higher – to apply when using fuel, ensuring the calculation reflects your specific energy use scenario.

When modeling your energy sources in Model Energy Flows, you can now specify the Energy Sourcing Type for each source: either Self-Generated (such as on-site solar) or Purchased (such as grid electricity or energy acquired from a supplier). When adding emission factor periods, the app visualizes the resulting energy and fuel mix as donut charts broken down by calculation method (location-based and market-based) for both Scope 1 and Scope 2, making it easy to spot gaps in your energy mix data before they affect calculation quality. A new import template for energy sources also supports bulk data maintenance.

Model Energy Source: Energy Mix Breakdown

The enriched data flows through to Manage Footprint Results, which now shows Energy Use in MWh for energy source input items alongside fuel mix or electricity mix breakdowns depending on the source type. In the Footprint Overview app, a dedicated Energy section provides consumption charts analyzed by source type and plant location, with renewable versus fossil subcategory views – supporting data quality monitoring and renewable energy adoption tracking across your organization.

For more information, see Enhancements to Energy Sources Using Energy Mix, Energy Content, and Fuel Mix on SAP Help. To see the energy source configuration and the resulting mix visualisations in practice, watch the short demo:

 

The richer energy data captured in SAP Sustainability Footprint Management also lays the groundwork for a tighter integration with SAP Sustainability Control Tower, which already supports detailed energy reporting for sustainability frameworks including CSRD. The ability to flow energy consumption data – in MWh, broken down by mix, sourcing type, and plant – directly from SAP Sustainability Footprint Management into SAP Sustainability Control Tower is planned for Q1 2027, enabling more automated energy disclosures with less need for manual data enrichment.

 

Default Sea Distances for Transport Footprint Calculations

Sea freight is a major source of transport emissions for many organizations, and the accuracy of Scope 3.4 and Scope 3.9 calculations depends on using distances that reflect actual shipping routes rather than theoretical straight-line paths. With the newly introduced pre-calculated sea distances between seaports – based on real commercial shipping lanes – as default content in the Manage Transport Activities app, we’re making transport footprint calculations for sea more accurate out of the box.

The default sea distances are computed using SCGraph, an open-source Python library for shortest-path routing across navigable sea networks, applying Dijkstra's algorithm across a global waypoint graph to produce the Shortest Feasible Distance (SFD) between seaport pairs in line with the GLEC Framework. To ensure routes follow commercially plausible shipping lanes – rather than theoretical shortest paths that might cross non-commercial routes such as Arctic passages – the routing graph was validated against Distances Between Ports (Pub. 151), published by the US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. The result is a set of SAP-delivered default sea legs that reflect real-world commercial shipping practice.

Shortest Feasible Distance in Transport Footprint Calculation

In practice, when the system generates routes and legs for a transport activity with sea as the main mode of transport, it identifies the nearest seaports to the source and target locations and uses the pre-calculated default distance for the sea leg directly – with no adjustment factor applied, since the SFD already accounts for the actual route. For all other transport modes, the great circle distance plus a configured adjustment factor continues to apply. For more information, see Manage Transport Activities and Generating Routes and Legs on SAP Help.

 

Customer-Driven Usability Improvements

Usability improvements don't always get the spotlight, but they often have the most immediate impact on daily work. Making the product genuinely easier to use is something we work on continuously, and this quarter, we added a set of targeted usability improvements – all driven directly by customer feedback submitted through the SAP Influence Portal. If you have feedback of your own, that is the right place to raise it. An improved Customer Influence experience is launching on October 6, more details to follow.

In the Manage Footprint Results app, you can now filter footprint items of type Product by Product Group and Product Type, making it easier to narrow down results without depending on other individual product characteristics.

Product Group and Product Type in Footprint Results

The Manage Emission Factors app now allows you to add comments when creating or editing an emission factor data package – a free-text field supporting up to 5,000 characters, useful for capturing internal references, sourcing details, or version-specific notes. For more information, see Creating Data Packages and Importing Emission Factors on SAP Help.

The Waste Generated in Operations app now displays a subtotal row at the end of each group in the table, showing the combined Waste Quantity and Total Footprint values for all entries within that group. This means you can see each group's total contribution without manually adding the individual rows. For more information, see Analyzing Footprints for Waste Generated in Operations on SAP Help.

 

Other Release Highlights

Default emission factor packages in the Manage Emission Factors app will now be updated on a fixed twice-yearly schedule, with releases in Q2 and Q4. If an update from a data provider is not available during a designated review period, it is deferred to the next cycle. For more information, see Default Emission Factor Data Packages on SAP Help.

On the API side, a new OData API for Transport Footprints is now available, allowing you to retrieve the list of transport footprints calculated as part of a footprint inventory scope over a given period. You can use the results to assess, analyze, and optimize your organization's transport-related environmental impacts programmatically. Find the Transport Footprints API on SAP Business Accelerator Hub; for more information, also see APIs for Analytics on SAP Help.

Furthermore, SAP Sustainability Footprint Management is now available in Italian, joining the existing set of supported languages and expanding the solution's reach for Italian-speaking users. For the full list of supported languages, see Supported Languages on SAP Help.

 

Upcoming Live Sessions

Reading about new features is one thing – whether you're a customer looking for a structured walkthrough, a partner seeking implementation depth, or simply want to put your questions directly to the product team, there are three upcoming live sessions worth putting on your calendar.

For partners, the next edition of the SAP Sustainability Footprint Management Meet the Expert Session takes place on October 7, 2026. This one-hour partner-exclusive deep dive offers a direct line to the experts behind the solution. Beyond product updates, you'll hear key learnings from real implementation projects and get the opportunity to submit your questions in advance or ask them live during the session. It is an ideal format for consultants and project managers who want insights that go beyond standard documentation: Register now.

For a broader portfolio view, the SAP Business Suite Product Expert Training (PET) H2 2026 is SAP's biannual flagship enablement event for partners – and for the first time, customers are also welcome to join. It covers the full breadth of the SAP Business Suite portfolio across product areas from Finance and Risk to Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and more. The H2 2026 edition runs from September 28 to October 16 in a hybrid format combining onsite and virtual sessions. The Sustainability Management and Carbon Accounting slot takes place on October 16, 2026 and covers the latest developments across SAP Sustainability Control Tower, SAP Sustainability Footprint Management, and SAP Sustainability Data Exchange in a one-hour session. It’s a practical way for partners and customers alike to stay current across the full carbon accounting portfolio in one go. Find the full PET program and register for the sustainability session on the SAP Business Suite Product Expert Training page, or go directly to the Sustainability Management and Carbon Accounting – PET H2 2026 session page.

Finally, on October 19, 2026, for the first time we're running a dedicated SAP Learning Live session: SAP Sustainability Footprint Management 2026 Q3 Release Highlights. This one-hour online session will walk through the key innovations delivered this quarter – what changed, where to find it in the product, and what it means for your day-to-day work. It also includes a live Q&A and is aimed at Sales, Presales, Consultants, and Business Users. Note that this session is part of the SAP Learning Hub offering and requires a subscription to access. The session runs in both a morning and afternoon slot (CET) to accommodate different time zones: View the schedule and register here.

 

Additional Information

entry.title: How to Navigate Packaging Regulations with SAP Responsible Design and Production
entry.content:
Why Packaging Regulation Matters

The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) introduces requirements that affect how companies design, manage, and document their packaging. Understanding these requirements and having the right data available is essential for supporting compliance and improving packaging transparency.

SAP Responsible Design and Production helps organizations manage packaging data and support processes related to regulatory requirements, making it easier to connect packaging information with compliance needs.

With SAP Responsible Design and Production, businesses can:

  • Understand and address PPWR requirements
  • Improve the quality and transparency of packaging data
  • Support packaging compliance processes
  • Organize the data and evidence needed for regulatory requirements
  • Integrate compliance considerations into packaging management

What You'll Learn in This Course

This beginner-level, 1.5-hour course introduces the PPWR and explains how SAP Responsible Design and Production supports related business processes.

  1. Understanding the PPWR Explore the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation and its potential impact on businesses.
  2. Translating Requirements into Packaging Data Learn about key PPWR requirements and how they translate into packaging data and supporting evidence.
  3. Applying SAP Responsible Design and Production Discover how to use SAP Responsible Design and Production to manage packaging data and support PPWR-related processes.

Who Should Take the Course?

This course is ideal for:

  • Business Users
  • Consultants
  • Sales and Presales

Recommended prerequisite: Administering and Using Responsible Design and Production for the Circular Economy.

Conclusion

Build your understanding of packaging regulations and discover how SAP can support your compliance processes and explore the course “Positioning Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation with SAP Responsible Design and Production” here.

entry.title: SAP Green Ledger: Q3-26 Release Updates and Highlights
entry.content:
Welcome to the Q3 2026 edition of our SAP Green Ledger Quarterly Release Highlights! This blog summarizes the most important innovations and enhancements delivered for SAP Green Ledger during Q3 2026.

This quarter brought several new capabilities and enhancements to SAP Green Ledger, including faster master data imports with delta loads, new APIs for integrating carbon data from external sources, carbon allocations from energy flows, and more flexible GHG analysis. Further enhancements improve CBAM liability management and usability.

Read on to learn more about the key innovations introduced throughout Q3 2026: 

  • Faster Master Data Imports with Delta Loads 
  • API-Based Carbon Data Imports 
  • Enhanced Carbon Data Import Details
  • Carbon Allocations from Energy Flows
  • WBS Elements for Manual Journal Entries 
  • Enhanced Carbon Liability Management 
  • More Flexible GHG Analysis in the Carbon Data Dashboard 
  • Enhanced Carbon and Financial Analysis in the Analytical Dashboard 
  • Further Updates and Enhancements

 

Faster Master Data Imports with Delta Loads

The Manage Master Data Imports app now supports delta loads in addition to full loads when importing master data from a connected SAP S/4HANA system, enabling faster and more efficient master data imports. Instead of importing the complete master data scope with every import, a delta load imports only newly created and changed master data objects since the previous full or delta load. This reduces the amount of data that needs to be processed and can significantly shorten the time required for the import.

Delta Load Option for Master Data Import from Connected SAP S/4HANA System

Delta loads are currently supported for account, account hierarchy, product, and project master data in both SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition. For cost center master data, delta loads are currently supported for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Other master data objects continue to be imported in full, even when the import is started as a delta load. The first master data import is always performed as a full load. A full load may also be required for subsequent imports, for example when changes are made to the relevant business system.

For more information, see SAP Help: Import Master Data.

 

API-Based Carbon Data Imports

SAP Green Ledger now provides three APIs for importing and processing carbon data from external sources. In addition to importing emission data from external sources via CSV files, the new APIs now provide a defined interface for integrating this data into SAP Green Ledger. The APIs support the different steps of the carbon data import process, from importing carbon data to releasing an import and monitoring its processing status.

The Carbon Data Import API allows you to import carbon data and create the data for the corresponding carbon collections. The Carbon Data Import Release API can then be used to release an import and trigger the creation of the corresponding carbon collections and journal entries. To monitor the process, the Carbon Data Import Status API provides information about the status of an import and the processing results of the corresponding carbon collections.

For more information, see the API Guide for SAP Green Ledger.

 

Enhanced Carbon Data Import Details

Once carbon data has been imported into SAP Green Ledger, it is important to understand how the data has been processed and what resulted from the import.

The Manage Carbon Data Imports app now provides more detailed information about your carbon data imports. You can review the imported data as well as the carbon collections and journal entries created from an import and navigate between them. This provides greater transparency into the results of a carbon data import and makes it easier to trace the imported data through to the resulting carbon collections and journal entries. The enhanced overview and navigation are available for new carbon data imports; existing imports remain unchanged.

Carbon Collections and Journal Entry Line Items from a Carbon Data Import

For more information, see SAP Help: Import Material Movements.

 

Carbon Allocations from Energy Flows

Energy flow models in SAP Sustainability Footprint Management represent how energy and the associated emissions are distributed across different elements of an organization. SAP Green Ledger now brings this information into carbon accounting to reflect the corresponding carbon allocations between cost centers. To support this, the import of modeled energy flows from SAP Sustainability Footprint Management has been extended. In addition to carbon emissions for energy sources, emissions for other nodes in the energy flow, such as facilities, meters, resources, and process infrastructures, are now also imported.

Using the Manage Carbon Data Imports app, you can import and release energy flows from a connected SAP Sustainability Footprint Management system. The imported data includes the cost center assignments of the individual nodes, which are carried into the corresponding carbon collections. When these carbon collections are posted to the journal, SAP Green Ledger creates the corresponding cost center-to-cost center allocations based on the modeled energy flow. The resulting journal entries include the respective cost centers and partner cost centers.

The carbon collections and resulting journal entries can be reviewed in the Manage Carbon Collections and Manage Journal Entries apps.

For more information, see SAP Help: Import Energy Flows.

 

WBS Elements for Manual Journal Entries

Carbon adjustments and corrections can now also be assigned to specific WBS elements when journal entries are created manually. The Manage Journal Entries app now supports WBS elements and partner WBS elements for manual journal entries.

When creating a manual journal entry, you can now assign a WBS element to a line item for eligible accounts. Cost center and WBS element are mutually exclusive and cannot be maintained for the same line item. When a WBS element is selected, the corresponding profit center and segment are automatically derived.

The WBS element value help displays WBS elements based on the relevant project and profit center context. The system also checks whether the selected WBS element is available for posting and informs you if any posting restrictions apply.

For more information, see SAP Help: Create Journal Entries.

 

Enhanced Carbon Liability Management

With the EU CBAM definitive regime in effect since January 2026, imports of certain goods into the European Union can result in carbon liabilities that need to be recognized and valued. SAP Green Ledger supports this process by accounting for the embedded emissions and the resulting carbon liabilities and by determining their fair value based on the corresponding certificate requirements and Emissions Trading System (ETS) prices. In Q3 2026, new enhancements provide further support for the valuation and review of these liabilities.

Official EU ETS Prices

The Configure Carbon Certificate Data app now displays the official quarterly ETS prices published by the European Union. These prices are automatically imported into SAP Green Ledger and used for the fair value calculation of carbon liabilities associated with imports subject to EU CBAM. You can view the official quarterly prices together with your maintained ETS prices in the Emissions Trading System Prices tab.

Official EU ETS Prices Imported for Quarter 1 and 2

A color indicator shows whether ETS prices are available for the current year and quarter: green indicates that prices are maintained for all calendar weeks, while blue indicates that the automatically imported official quarterly EU ETS prices are used.

For more information, see SAP Help: View and Maintain Emissions Trading System Prices.

Product Information in Carbon Liabilities

The Manage Carbon Liabilities app now displays the Product selected for carbon collections that require carbon certificates, providing additional context when reviewing carbon liabilities.

For more information, see SAP Help: View Carbon Liabilities and Create a Carbon Collection.

 

More Flexible GHG Analysis in the Carbon Data Dashboard 

The Carbon Data Dashboard has been enhanced with new options for analyzing GHG emissions. 

The timing of GHG emission recognition can differ depending on whether emissions are considered when carbon data is posted or when the underlying resources are actually consumed. You can now choose between the accrual and non-accrual accounting method, which determines how GHG emissions are calculated and displayed in the dashboard. 

With the non-accrual method, GHG emissions are recognized when carbon-relevant data is posted to the GHG Liabilities Collection account. The resulting GHG emissions therefore represent the emissions recorded at the time of the carbon data posting, regardless of subsequent activities related to the underlying resources. 

With the accrual method, emissions are distinguished based on whether the underlying resources have already been consumed. Emissions related to consumed resources are recognized as realized GHG emissions in profit and loss accounts, while emissions related to resources that have not yet been consumed remain as accrued emissions in balance sheet accounts. As the resources are consumed, the corresponding emissions move from the balance sheet to profit and loss. This allows the dashboard to reflect GHG emissions in line with actual resource consumption.

Selection of Accrued and Non-Accrued GHG Emissions Overview

The Carbon Data Dashboard also introduces an enhancement to the WBS Element filter. The filter is now organized by project, with a project node at the top of the hierarchy grouping the corresponding WBS elements. This provides clearer context and makes it easier to locate and select WBS elements within their associated projects.

Enhanced WBS Element Filter Organized by Project

 For more information, see SAP Help: Analyze Carbon Data and Accounting Method.

 

Enhanced Carbon and Financial Analysis in the Analytical Dashboard 

The SAP Green Ledger Analytical Dashboard has also been updated for Q3 2026 with enhancements to filtering and data visualization. The updates make it easier to analyze carbon data in the context of projects and WBS elements and further improve the presentation and interpretation of GHG and financial data. 

For a detailed overview of the latest SAP Green Ledger Analytical Dashboard enhancements, see the dedicated SAP Community blog post and the SAP Help Portal topic Analyze Carbon Data Alongside Financial Data.

 

Further Updates and Enhancements

Several smaller enhancements further improve the usability of SAP Green Ledger. 

Line Item Totals and Subtotals 

The Line Items table in the Manage Journal Entries app now displays debit and credit totals and subtotals. When line items are grouped by an attribute, you can view the corresponding subtotals for each group, making it easier to analyze and review carbon-related postings. 

Filtering by Empty Dimension Values 

The Manage Journal Entries, Display Line Items, and Display Account Balances apps now allow you to filter for empty or unassigned values across supported dimensions, including, for example, WBS element, cost center, product, and supplier. You can display only postings where a particular dimension has not been assigned, or exclude these postings from the results. This makes it easier to review postings based on whether specific dimension information is available. 

Journal Entry IDs Without Leading Zeros 

Journal entry IDs are now displayed without leading zeros across SAP Green Ledger, making them easier to read, search, and sort. This applies wherever journal entry IDs are displayed. 

Documentation Feedback on SAP Help Portal

You can now provide feedback directly on the Admin Guide, Integration Guide, API Guide, and Introduction for SAP Green Ledger on SAP Help Portal. This makes it easier to share feedback on specific documentation content directly from the page you are viewing. For more information, see SAP Help: Giving Documentation Feedback on SAP Help Portal.

 

Additional Information 

If you want to dive deeper into SAP Green Ledger, the SAP Help Portal is a good place to start. It provides detailed information on concepts, configuration, and application usage. You can also check the What’s New section, which is updated with every release and gives a complete overview of the latest additions. To see what's coming next, the SAP Road Map Explorer offers insight into planned features and upcoming innovations. It is updated regularly and outlines how the solution will continue to evolve.

entry.title: New Enablement Resources for SAP Sustainability Control Tower
entry.content:
Getting started with a new solution involves more than understanding its individual features. Project teams need guidance throughout the implementation, while new users and consultants need accessible learning resources that help them build a solid understanding of the solution.

To support both needs, new enablement materials for SAP Sustainability Control Tower are now available: the End-to-End Implementation Guide and the Learning Journey for SAP Sustainability Control Tower.

While the Implementation Guide is intended to provide guidance throughout an end-to-end implementation project, the Learning Journey offers a structured way to become familiar with SAP Sustainability Control Tower and build foundational knowledge.

Guidance Along the Implementation Journey

The SAP Sustainability Control Tower End-to-End Implementation Guide was created to support project teams throughout an implementation. It is a comprehensive guide for ESG projects with SAP Sustainability Control Tower.

Rather than looking at individual implementation topics in isolation, its purpose is to provide guidance along the implementation journey and give project teams a central reference as they work with SAP Sustainability Control Tower.

At a high level, the implementation guidance covers areas around:

  • Getting started with SAP Sustainability Control Tower and preparing for implementation
  • Setting up and administering the solution
  • Data Acquisition (quantitative and qualitative)
  • Working with sustainability data and business scenarios
  • Using reporting and disclosure features

These themes align with SAP Help's overall implementation resources for SAP Sustainability Control Tower, which include setup and administration, security, integrations, application guidance and business scenarios.

Explore the SAP Sustainability Control Tower End-to-End Implementation Guide

Build Your SAP Sustainability Control Tower Knowledge

The Learning Journey, Reporting and Steering Sustainability in Your Businesses Using SAP Sustainability Control Tower, complements the implementation guidance by providing structured learning content.

It is designed especially for business users who are new to SAP Sustainability Control Tower as well as consultants who want to build their knowledge of the solution. The course is classified as beginner level, with no prerequisites.

The Learning Journey takes learners through the solution step by step, covering:

  • Positioning and architecture of SAP Sustainability Control Tower
  • Fundamentals of the solution
  • Business configuration
  • Data collection
  • Data imports and system integrations
  • Reporting and analysis of sustainability metrics
  • Turning insights into action, including ambitions and targets

Together, these topics provide a structured introduction to the solution, from understanding its foundations to working with data, analysing sustainability metrics and acting on the results. The course is organised into seven units and is specifically aimed at enabling consultants and business users to set up and use SAP Sustainability Control Tower.

Start the SAP Learning course: Reporting and Steering Sustainability in Your Businesses Using SAP Sustainability Control Tower

Two Resources, One Goal: Making It Easier to Get Started

Together, the End-to-End Implementation Guide and Learning Journey provide two complementary entry points into SAP Sustainability Control Tower enablement.

If you are approaching the solution from an implementation perspective, the End-to-End Implementation Guide can accompany you throughout your ESG project journey. If your priority is to build your knowledge of the solution, the Learning Journey provides a structured starting point and takes you through the key areas of SAP Sustainability Control Tower.

Depending on your role and experience, you can use the materials individually or combine them: build your foundational knowledge through the Learning Journey and use the End-to-End Implementation Guide as a reference as you move into an implementation project.

We hope these new enablement resources provide valuable support throughout your learning and implementation journey with SAP Sustainability Control Tower.

 
Special kudos to Alexander Zunic, Lara Loehrke, Cosma Urban, Johannes Müller, Shweta Kanwar, Mirella Baita-Burman and Anitha Rani, whose contributions to the implementation guide and/or learning journey helped bring these resources to life.
